history.summary: FLAG - IDENTITY UNCERTAIN / PROVISIONAL RECORD. No distinct 'Ganga Lake Temple' could be verified on the web: travel guides describe Ganga Lake (also Gyakar Sinyi / Geykar Sinyi) purely as a scenic forest lake about 6 km from Itanagar in the Ganga area, surrounded by primeval vegetation, orchids and tree ferns - none lists a temple at the lake. Generic 'Shiv Mandir' map listings exist in the vicinity but none is a documented 'Ganga Lake Temple'. This file is therefore kept as a provisional record anchored to the lake's location; the media image shows the lake itself, not a temple. Note: CSV row 51 'Ganga Mata Mandir, Naharlagun' is a separate entry and should not be merged here. If Mahesh can confirm the intended shrine, this record needs revision.

name: Ganga Lake Temple
town_description: Itanagar is the capital of Arunachal Pradesh (since 20 April 1974), at the foothills of the Himalayas in Papum Pare district, identified with Mayapur of the 14th-15th century. It is known for Itafort (the brick fort that gives the city its name), the Buddhist Gompa, the Jawaharlal Nehru State Museum, and Ganga Lake (Gyakar Sinyi), a popular picnic spot about 6 km away.
tradition: Unverified (flag: no documented temple at Ganga Lake; provisional record)
